text:
sam: quick note — new angle on client surface: ship a tiny local shim (edge-proxy) that does REST/gRPC -> internal protobuf, header consistency, and a small token pre-alloc cache. aim: reduce control-plane trips and make console quotas + rollouts deterministic.

priya: short Q: how is this different from the gateway-adapter we've kicked around? sounds close.

sam: difference is responsibility split. gateway = policy authority and enforcement. shim = translation + transient token cache + batching/backpressure hints. shim never makes final quota decisions.

lee: that keeps the single source of truth for billing/quotas. but ops will want visibility into shim behavior — dropped batches, prealloc grants, etc. how do we surface that?

marcus: console changes: add an "edge-health" panel per-tenant showing shim cache hit rate, prealloc grant rates, and locally observed burst size distribution. pair with per-route quota burn rate.

evan: customers on REST-only integrations — will they need to change anything?

sam: no. shim exposes same REST endpoints and translates internally to proto over mTLS. SDKs just talk to local shim.

priya: token pre-alloc flow? explain briefly.

sam: flow: SDK asks shim for tokens when it wants to batch. shim consults its local bucket; if insufficient and TTL expired it calls quota service: `POST /quota/alloc {tenant, route, tokens}`. service replies `{granted}`. shim caches grants with a small TTL and drains locally.

lee: need example curl and TTL values for ops docs.

marcus: example: 
```
curl -X POST https://quota.redwood.internal/alloc -H "Authorization: Bearer <svc>" -d '{"tenant":"t-123","route":"inference","tokens":50}'
# response: {"granted":42}
```
TTL suggestion: 5s coarse TTL for small tenants, 1s for hot tenants (adaptive).

priya: bursts still possible. what about worst-case where SDKs across many hosts pre-alloc and spike?

sam: two mitigations: 1) gateway enforces a hard global windowed limiter per-tenant; 2) shim respects a soft remote budget that the quota service can set dynamically (e.g., reduce grants if close to cap).

lee: header contract needs to be stable. propose minimal required headers from shim -> gateway: `x-rdw-tenant`, `x-rdw-route`, `x-rdw-reqid`, `x-rdw-canary` (optional). also pass through `x-forwarded-for`.

marcus: telemetry labels: service, tenant, route, model_version, shard, canary_bucket. console alerting will use these tags to compare baseline vs canary.

priya: rolling canaries: we should support both percent-of-traffic and percent-of-tenants. UX: slider + target dimension drop-down. auto-rollback triggers: 95th latency increase > 20%, error rate spike > 0.5%, embedding-similarity drift > 0.08.

evan: embedding drift — we need instrumentation. where do golden prompts live and how often do we run them?

sam: Redwood Optimize will host a small eval job per rollout. run every 5m in canary windows, compute cosine similarity vs baseline. tie threshold to rollout gate.

lee: proto schema stability: require strict rules: add new fields with high numbers, avoid type changes, deprecate only. publish canonical proto and a JSON mapping for debug. clients may set `Accept-Proto-Version` header to request compat behavior.

priya: propose a light compatibility checker in CI that tests wasm/node/python SDKs against the proto.

marcus: perf targets: shim translation median <1ms, p95 <4ms co-located sidecar. token-check local cache should avoid >90% control-plane calls. add perf counters to telemetry.

evan: retention and cost conversation: infra wants short retention for traces; product wants long for longitudinal quality. compromise: aggregated metrics 180d, request-level traces 14d, golden-eval outputs 365d. premium tiers can extend trace retention.

lee: security notes: shim authenticates to gateway with mTLS. keys come from customer KMS or Redwood-managed KMS per deployment model. log key rotations into console and expose a rotation alert.

priya: billing forecast: console should present projected monthly spend based on current batching and quantization settings and show delta if customer toggles more aggressive batching/quant.

marcus: sample query for canary vs baseline token latency: `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(token_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, canary_bucket))` — console will render side-by-side.

sam: short proto snippet for docs: 
```
syntax = "proto3";
message EdgeRequest {
  string tenant = 1;
  string route = 2;
  bytes payload = 3; // UTF-8 JSON or model binary
  map<string,string> meta = 4;
}
```

evan: ops-bot: created issue #edge-shim-123 with checklist -> proto spec, shim binary + unit tests, token-service, console panels, canary automation.

priya: i'll take console panels and rollout UI work.

lee: i'll prototype shim and header propagation. evan pick token service?

evan: yep i'll own quota service and audit logs.

sam: timeline: prototype in 2 weeks, internal beta (opt-in tenants) in 5 weeks. objections?

marcus: one small ask — include a debug endpoint on shim protected by admin token to dump its cache state for troubleshooting.

sam: ack. will add `/admin/diag` behind RBAC.

infra-bot: RFC created https://rdrw.internal/rfc/1299 assigned sam/lee/priya/marcus/evan.

marcus: thanks all. if nobody objects i'll open RFC and tracking tickets. :rocket:
